mainTopic: Covering ערוה and filth so one may recite קריאת שמע, and keeping holy objects covered
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree about urine that is wet enough to wet other things. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about a בעל קרי who goes down to immerse before reciting שמע. It shows that the משנה can follow רבי יהושע, because the sunrise deadline may reflect the practice of the ותיקין. The גמרא also explains that covering oneself in water works only with murky water, so that his heart does not 'see' his ערוה. It rules that a heel touching the ערוה is forbidden, while a heel seeing it is permitted. רבא teaches that a see-through cover works for צואה but not for ערוה, and the ערוה of a גוי also forbids קריאת שמע. The גמרא then discusses foul water, urine and chamber pots: how much water must be added, where the pot may stand, and how high a bed must be to separate what is under it. It ends with the story of רב אחאי and a ספר תורה in the wedding room, and the rule of a container inside a container, which רבא's statement about a cloak continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The practical difference: moist enough to make other things wet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. It says the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree about urine that is moist enough to wet something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, the difference between them is a case where the urine is moist enough to make other things moist.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an earlier discussion. The גמרא names the exact case where the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי would rule differently about urine on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions forbid saying holy words near moist urine. The question is how moist it must be. The תנא קמא forbids it only when the urine is wet enough to wet other things. רבי יוסי forbids it as long as the urine itself is still wet, even if it cannot wet anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet enough to make something else wet
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree only about how wet the urine must be for the איסור to apply.

phrases.english: And here, in a case where it is moist
phrases.notes: This finishes a discussion that started before this section. 'Here' means the case of urine.

phrases.english: enough to moisten other things,
there is a difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּטוֹפֵחַ עַל מְנָת לְהַטְפִּיחַ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section, about what the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when the urine is wet enough to wet other things.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is only about the degree of wetness.

steps.title: Does the unattributed משנה follow רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a person who goes down to immerse and must judge whether he can come up and recite שמע before sunrise. It asks: does this mean the משנה follows רבי אליעזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if one went down to immerse, he must judge whether he can come up and recite in time. Shall we say the unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who said שמע may be recited until sunrise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. It suggests that this line seems to follow only רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats sunrise as the deadline for reciting שמע. That matches רבי אליעזר's view that the time for שמע ends at sunrise. רבי יהושע allows reciting until the third hour of the day. So it seems the unattributed משנה sides with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He went down to immerse in a מקוה
Shall we say? (it introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing)
The תנא taught it without naming whose opinion it is

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the law of immersing. It is about which תנא sets the deadline for שמע at sunrise.

phrases.english: One who went down to immerse,
if he is able to come up, etc.:
Shall we say the unattributed teaching
follows רבי אליעזר,
who said: until sunrise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה about immersing before קריאת שמע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה's sunrise deadline mean it follows only רבי אליעזר?

steps.title: It can follow רבי יהושע if it is speaking about the ותיקין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The משנה could follow רבי יהושע if it is speaking about the ותיקין, who made a point of reciting at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי יהושע, perhaps it is speaking about people who follow the practice of the ותיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 2. It shows the משנה does not have to follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sunrise deadline may not be the law for everyone. It may be the special practice of the ותיקין. The משנה could then agree with רבי יהושע's later deadline and simply be advising people who keep this special practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Very careful, pious people who did מצוות in the best possible way

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows רבי יהושע,
perhaps it follows the practice of the ותיקין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְדִלְמָא כְּוָתִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 2 that the משנה follows only רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sunrise deadline could be the practice of the ותיקין, not the basic law.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ותיקין finished שמע at sunrise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement supports step 3. The ותיקין finished saying שמע exactly at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: the ותיקין would finish it together with sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's statement. It shows that the 'practice of the ותיקין' from step 3 really was tied to sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ותיקין timed their שמע to end exactly at sunrise. For them, sunrise really was the deadline. So a משנה that warns a person to finish before sunrise fits their practice, even according to רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: They finish it (the reciting of שמע)
Together with, at the same moment as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the special practice of finishing קריאת שמע exactly at sunrise.

phrases.english: As רבי יוחנן said:
The ותיקין would finish it
together with sunrise.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וָתִיקִין הָיוּ גּוֹמְרִין אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 by explaining what the practice of the ותיקין was.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה could be speaking about the ותיקין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן: the ותיקין finished שמע at sunrise.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה can follow רבי יהושע, because the sunrise deadline is the practice of the ותיקין.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's sunrise deadline does not prove it follows רבי אליעזר. It may reflect the practice of the ותיקין.

steps.title: Covering in water: his heart still sees his nakedness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if he cannot come up in time, he covers himself in the water and recites. It challenges this, because his heart can still 'see' his nakedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and if not, he should cover himself in water and recite. But his heart sees his nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and raises a challenge against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water covers his body from other people's eyes. But nothing separates his heart from his own nakedness. A person may not recite שמע when 'his heart sees his nakedness.' So how can the משנה allow reciting while standing in the water?

keyTerms.meaning: He should cover himself with the water
His heart sees his nakedness; nothing separates the heart from the body below it

steps.confusionAlert: Clear water does not cover his body from view, so water alone is not a barrier between his heart and his nakedness.

phrases.english: And if not,
he should cover himself in the water and recite.
But his heart sees his nakedness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the same משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that he may cover himself in water and recite.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water does not separate his heart from his nakedness, and reciting שמע is forbidden when the heart sees the ערוה.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about murky water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (or רבי אחא בר אבא בר אחא in the name of רב) answers that the משנה speaks of murky water. Murky water is like thick earth, so his heart does not 'see' his ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said, and some say it was רבי אחא בר אבא בר אחא in the name of our teacher: They taught this about murky water, which is like thick earth, so his heart does not see his nakedness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5 by narrowing the משנה to murky water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked how covering oneself in water helps if the heart can still 'see' the ערוה through it. The answer is that murky water blocks the view the way solid ground does. So it acts as a real barrier between the heart and the ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart 'sees' his nakedness, meaning nothing separates the upper body from the ערוה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא בַּר אַחָא
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Acha bar Abba bar Acha
in the name of our teacher:
They taught this about murky water,
which is like thick earth,
so that his heart does not see his nakedness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא בַּר אַחָא מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the משנה refers only to murky water.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any water counts, so the heart would still see the ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Murky water acts like solid earth and separates the heart from the ערוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about clear water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in clear water one sits up to his neck and recites. The יש אומרים say he must first make the water murky with his foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In clear water, he sits in it up to his neck and recites. And some say: he makes it murky with his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same topic, now about clear water, and this sets up the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion seems to allow reciting even in see-through water. The יש אומרים require stirring up the water, which matches the idea from step 6 that only murky water is a barrier. The next steps ask how the first תנא can allow clear water.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear water you can see through
He stirs it up and makes it murky with his foot
'Some say,' a second opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Clear water:
he sits in it up to his neck and recites.
And some say: he makes it murky with his foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about clear water, after step 6 dealt with murky water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: in clear water one sits up to the neck and recites. יש אומרים: he must make the water murky with his foot first.

steps.title: Doesn't his heart see the ערוה in clear water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first תנא: in clear water, his heart sees the ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא: but his heart sees the nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion in the ברייתא, which allows reciting in clear water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clear water does not block anything. So the problem from steps 5 and 6, that the heart sees the ערוה, should apply here. How can the first תנא allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And the first תנא:
but his heart sees the nakedness!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא קַמָּא, וַהֲרֵי לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first opinion in the ברייתא from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא's ruling that one may recite in clear water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clear water is no barrier, so the heart sees the ערוה, which should forbid reciting.

steps.title: The first תנא allows 'heart sees ערוה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first תנא holds that when the heart sees the ערוה, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that when his heart sees the nakedness, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first תנא simply disagrees with the concern about the heart seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not make the problem go away. It says the first תנא has a different view: 'heart sees ערוה' is not a reason to forbid. So the two opinions in the ברייתא disagree about exactly this point.

phrases.english: He holds that when his heart sees the nakedness,
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the first תנא holds a different rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that 'heart sees ערוה' forbids reciting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא holds that 'heart sees ערוה' is permitted.

steps.title: Doesn't his heel see the ערוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: in clear water, his heel also sees the ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But his heel sees the nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the first תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in clear water, there is also nothing between his heel and his ערוה. This is a different problem from the heart. Maybe this should still forbid reciting.

phrases.english: But his heel sees the nakedness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the first תנא, after step 9 answered the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא's ruling allowing clear water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if 'heart sees' is allowed, the heel also sees the ערוה with nothing between them.

steps.title: The first תנא also allows 'heel sees ערוה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first תנא also holds that when the heel sees the ערוה, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that when his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer: the first תנא allows this case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the answer is that the first תנא holds a lenient rule. Now we know he allows both 'heart sees' and 'heel sees.' This sets up the next discussion about the heel.

keyTerms.meaning: His heel 'sees,' meaning nothing separates the heel from the ערוה

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: He holds that when his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the first תנא holds a lenient rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא holds that 'heel sees ערוה' is permitted.

steps.title: רב זביד's version: they argue about a heel that touches
steps.stepSummary: It was stated: a heel that sees the ערוה is permitted. About a heel that touches it, אביי forbids and רבא permits. This is how רב זביד taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: When his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted. When it touches: אביי said it is forbidden, and רבא said it is permitted. רב זביד taught this teaching this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between אביי and רבא about the heel, in the version taught by רב זביד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version everyone agrees that 'heel sees' is permitted. The argument is only about the heel actually touching the ערוה. אביי is strict and רבא is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated,' introducing a statement of the אמוראים
'Taught it this way,' giving one version of a teaching

phrases.english: It was stated:
When his heel sees the nakedness, it is permitted;
when it touches:
Abaye said: it is forbidden,
and Rava said: it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד מַתְנִי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא הָכִי.
phrases.english: Rav Zevid taught this teaching this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: עֲקֵבוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11's 'heel sees is permitted' and asks about touching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heel sees ערוה: permitted. Heel touches ערוה: אביי forbids, רבא permits.

steps.title: רב חיננא's version: they argue about a heel that sees
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא taught it differently. Touching is forbidden by everyone. They argue about seeing: אביי forbids and רבא permits, because the Torah was not given to angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא son of רב איקא taught it this way: When it touches, everyone agrees it is forbidden. When it sees: אביי said it is forbidden, רבא said it is permitted, because the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same מחלוקת, which moves the argument to an earlier point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now touching is forbidden according to everyone. The argument is about 'heel sees,' where אביי is strict. רבא explains why he is lenient: people have bodies, and the Torah does not demand what only angels could do.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah was not given to the ministering angels; it was given to human beings

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not argue about the same case. In רב זביד's version they argue about touching. In רב חיננא's version they argue about seeing.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מַתְנִי לַהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Chinnana, son of Rav Ika, taught it this way:
When it touches, everyone agrees it is forbidden;
when it sees:
Abaye said: it is forbidden,
Rava said: it is permitted:
the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מַתְנִי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the מחלוקת from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching: forbidden by all. Seeing: אביי forbids, רבא permits because the Torah was not given to angels.

steps.title: Final הלכה: touching is forbidden, seeing is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that a heel touching the ערוה is forbidden, and a heel seeing the ערוה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: touching is forbidden, seeing is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching is forbidden. That is how everyone rules in רב חיננא's version, and it follows אביי in רב זביד's version. Seeing is permitted, following רבא's lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the הלכה is,' the final practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Murky water counts as a covering for קריאת שמע. For the heel, the final הלכה is: touching the ערוה is forbidden, seeing it is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for reciting שמע when the body is not covered, and it rests on the idea that the Torah was given to human beings, not angels.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
touching is forbidden,
seeing is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the מחלוקת from steps 12 and 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A heel touching the ערוה is forbidden. A heel seeing the ערוה is permitted.

steps.title: רבא: A see-through cover works for feces but not for nakedness
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that צואה under a transparent cover permits קריאת שמע, but ערוה under a transparent cover does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If צואה is under a see-through cover like a lantern, you may say קריאת שמע facing it. If ערוה is under a see-through cover, you may not say קריאת שמע facing it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling that treats צואה and ערוה differently when each is behind a clear, see-through cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same for both: something is covered, but you can still see it through the cover. Yet רבא gives opposite results. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: A lantern, meaning a clear, see-through covering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a cover always solves the problem. The same see-through cover helps for צואה but not for ערוה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Feces in a lantern,
phrases.notes: A lantern here means a clear covering, so the feces are covered but can still be seen.

phrases.english: it is permitted to read Shema facing it.
Nakedness in a lantern,
it is forbidden to read Shema facing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of a heel and ערוה and begins a new ruling about see-through coverings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A see-through cover is enough for צואה but not for ערוה.

steps.title: The reason: feces depends on covering, nakedness depends on being seen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבא's two rulings and gives the reason for each. צואה depends on covering, and ערוה depends on being seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: צואה under a clear cover is allowed, because for צואה everything depends on being covered, and here it is covered. ערוה under a clear cover is forbidden, because the תורה said, 'No ערוה shall be seen in you,' and here it is seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבא's two rulings and explains the source behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule comes from a different פסוק with a different key word. For צואה the פסוק says 'cover,' so being covered is enough even if it can be seen. For ערוה the פסוק says 'shall not be seen,' so what matters is whether it is visible.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two different standards: 'covered' for צואה and 'not seen' for ערוה. That difference explains many rulings about which barriers work for which problem.

phrases.english: Feces in a lantern
it is permitted to read Shema facing it
because with feces, the matter depends on covering,
and here it is covered.
Nakedness in a lantern
it is forbidden to read Shema facing it,
"And no indecent thing shall be seen in you"
the Merciful One said.
And here it is seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind each half of רבא's ruling in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צואה requires covering, and ערוה requires not being seen.

steps.title: A small amount of feces can be cancelled with spit
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a tiny bit of צואה can be cancelled by spitting on it. רבא adds that the spit must be thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A tiny amount of צואה can be cancelled by spitting on it. רבא said: Only with thick spit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a practical way to deal with a small amount of צואה, and רבא adds a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the idea that for צואה, covering is what counts. Spit can work as a cover for a tiny amount. רבא says it only works if the spit is thick enough to really cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels it, makes it not count

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A tiny amount of feces,
one cancels it with spit.
Rava said: And with thick spit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another practical way to cover צואה, following the idea that for צואה covering is what counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tiny amount of צואה can be cancelled with thick spit.

steps.title: Covering feces in a hole with a sandal
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if צואה is in a hole, putting a sandal over it is enough to say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If צואה is in a hole, he puts his sandal over it and says קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another simple way to cover צואה: put a sandal over the hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sandal works as a cover over the hole, so the צואה counts as covered. This again shows that for צואה, covering solves the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole or pit in the ground

phrases.english: Rava said:
Feces in a hole —
he places his sandal over it,
and reads Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical case of covering צואה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sandal over a hole with צואה counts as covering it.

steps.title: Feces stuck to the sandal: the question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא asks what the law is when צואה is stuck to the sandal itself. The question stays unanswered (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: מר son of רבינא asked: What if צואה is stuck to his sandal? Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the sandal case, the גמרא asks about צואה stuck to the sandal itself, and leaves the question with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the hole case, the sandal covers the צואה. Here the צואה is on the sandal itself, so it is not clear whether that counts as covered or not. The גמרא does not decide, and says תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Mar son of Ravina asked:
Feces stuck to his sandal — what is the law?
Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the sandal case from step 18 one step further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether צואה stuck to a sandal counts as covered.

steps.title: רב יהודה: No שמע facing a naked non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that it is forbidden to say קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is forbidden to say קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling about ערוה. The next steps question why he needed to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling extends the ban on ערוה to a non-Jew. Mentioning the גוי specifically will lead to the question in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A naked gentile —
it is forbidden to read Shema facing him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the subject of ערוה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערוה of a גוי forbids קריאת שמע facing it.

steps.title: Why mention a non-Jew? A Jew is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה mentioned a גוי, since a naked ישראל is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he mention a גוי specifically? Even a ישראל is also forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יהודה's ruling: why single out a גוי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is true for everyone, mentioning only a גוי seems unnecessary, or might suggest a ישראל is different. The גמרא wants to know the point of the detail.

phrases.english: Why specifically a gentile?
Even a Jew is also forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's choice to mention a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule applies to a ישראל too, so mentioning a גוי seems pointless.

steps.title: The non-Jew case was needed: their nakedness also counts
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל is obvious. The גוי case was needed so we would not think a גוי is like a donkey based on a פסוק. A פסוק about נח's sons shows their nakedness is also called ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a ישראל, it is obvious that it is forbidden. He needed to teach about a גוי. You might have thought that since a פסוק compares their flesh to donkeys' flesh, a גוי is just like a donkey. So he teaches that they are also called ערוה, as it says: 'and their father's ערוה they did not see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה had to mention a גוי because, without his ruling, we might have thought it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a possible mistake: a פסוק in יחזקאל compares them to donkeys, so we might treat their bodies like an animal's, which is not ערוה. A פסוק in בראשית about נח, who was not Jewish, calls his body ערוה, so the rule applies to non-Jews too.
steps.whatToRemember: The ערוה of a גוי also forbids קריאת שמע facing it. Only the case of a גוי needed to be stated; a ישראל was obvious.

phrases.english: A Jew, it is obvious to him that it is forbidden,
but a gentile, he needed to state.
You might have said,
since it is written about them,
"whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys,"
say he is just like a donkey,
so he teaches us
that they too are called nakedness,
as it is written: "And their father's nakedness they did not see."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:23. This is about נח, who lived before there were any Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׂרָאֵל פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּאָסוּר, אֶלָּא גּוֹי אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the detail was needed to rule out a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on יחזקאל, a גוי might be treated like a donkey, whose body is not ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Based on בראשית 9:23, the nakedness of non-Jews is also called ערוה.

steps.title: The משנה: Foul water and soaking water as a cover
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one may not cover himself with foul water or flax-soaking water until he pours water into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not cover himself with foul water or with flax-soaking water until he pours water into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the משנה seems to say that adding fresh water fixes foul or soaking water. The next step questions this.

phrases.english: And he may not cover himself
not with foul water
and not with soaking water
phrases.notes: This is water that flax was soaked in, which smells very bad.

phrases.english: until he pours water into them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the side discussions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foul water and soaking water cannot be used as a cover unless water is added.

steps.title: How much water would he have to keep pouring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much fresh water would be enough, since foul water and soaking water would need a huge amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much water would he have to keep on pouring?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the משנה: adding water to such strong water does not seem practical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foul water and soaking water usually come in large amounts and smell strongly. Fixing them would take endless pouring, so the plain reading does not make sense.

phrases.english: And how much water
does he keep on pouring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'until he pours water into them' applied to foul and soaking water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The amount of water needed would be far too large to be practical.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: Adding water only helps for urine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. Foul water and soaking water are never allowed. Adding water only helps for urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: He may not cover himself with foul water or soaking water at all. As for urine, once he pours water into it, he may say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה differently: the part about adding water belongs to a different case, urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foul water and soaking water are banned completely, so no amount of water helps. Urine is a smaller amount, so adding water to it is practical, and then he may say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatToRemember: Foul water and flax-soaking water can never be used as a cover for קריאת שמע. Urine is fine once water is poured into it.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it means:
He may not cover himself with foul water
nor with soaking water at all.
And urine:
once he pours water into it,
then he may read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Adding water fixes foul water and soaking water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Foul water and soaking water are never allowed. Adding water only helps for urine.

steps.title: How much water must be added to urine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. The תנא קמא says any amount of water is enough. רבי זכאי says a רביעית is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How much water must one pour into urine? Any amount. רבי זכאי says: a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that takes the rule from the last step, adding water to urine, and asks how much water is needed. Two answers are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 taught that adding water helps only for urine. Now we learn how much water that takes. The first opinion says any amount at all, while רבי זכאי requires a set measure called a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Any amount, even a tiny bit
A quarter of a לוג, a set liquid measure
He will pour or put in

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How much water must one pour into them?
Any amount.
Rabbi Zakkai says: a quarter.
phrases.notes: A quarter of a לוג, a known liquid measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּמָּה יָטִיל לְתוֹכָן מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 25 limited the 'pour in water' rule to urine. This ברייתא now asks a new question about it: how much water is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says any amount of water helps for urine. רבי זכאי says a רביעית is needed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the dispute is about water added afterward
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the dispute is only when water is poured in after the urine. If the water was in the pot first, any amount is enough according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The dispute is about water added at the end. But if the water is there at the beginning, any amount is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains which case the ברייתא's dispute is talking about. He limits the argument to one situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases: urine first and then water, or water first and then urine. רב נחמן says they argue only when the water comes after the urine. When the water is already waiting in the pot, everyone agrees any amount works.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end, meaning water added after the urine
At the beginning, meaning water already in the pot before the urine

steps.confusionAlert: "Beginning" and "end" here do not mean before or after reading שמע. They describe whether the water went into the pot before the urine or after it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The dispute is about afterward.
phrases.notes: He means the urine is already in the pot, and the water is poured in after it.

phrases.english: But at the beginning, any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which case the ברייתא in step 26 is arguing about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about water added after the urine. When the water is there first, any amount is enough.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the dispute is about water placed first
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the opposite. The dispute is about water placed in the pot first. When water is added after the urine, everyone agrees a רביעית is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: The dispute is about water at the beginning. But at the end, everyone agrees a רביעית is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different explanation of the same dispute. He flips רב נחמן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, the case of water first is the one in dispute. The case of water poured in after the urine is stricter, and there everyone requires a רביעית. So for רב יוסף, "any amount" is never enough when the water comes after the urine.

keyTerms.meaning: At the start. Here it means the water was put in before the urine.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
The dispute is about the beginning.
But afterward, everyone agrees: a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite explanation from רב נחמן in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about water placed first. When water is added after the urine, everyone requires a רביעית.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks for a רביעית of water
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף told his attendant to bring him a רביעית of water, following רבי זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to his attendant: Bring me a רביעית of water, as רבי זכאי says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how רב יוסף acted in real life. It shows which opinion he followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף held that the case of water placed first is the one in dispute. By asking for a full רביעית, he showed that he rules like רבי זכאי even in that case. So in practice he did not rely on "any amount."
steps.whatToRemember: There are two cases: water before urine and water after urine. רב נחמן and רב יוסף disagree about which case the dispute is about. רב יוסף himself followed רבי זכאי and used a רביעית.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to his attendant:
Bring me a quarter of water,
like Rabbi Zakkai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב יוסף, whose view was given in step 28, acted in practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף ruled like רבי זכאי in practice and used a רביעית of water.

steps.title: Chamber pots are forbidden even when empty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may not say קריאת שמע facing a chamber pot, even an empty one. Urine itself is allowed once water is added. The same dispute about the amount of water appears again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Facing a pot used for feces or a vessel used for urine, it is forbidden to read קריאת שמע, even if there is nothing in them. Facing urine itself, it is forbidden until he pours water into it. How much water? Any amount. רבי זכאי says: a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a longer ברייתא. It adds a new rule about the pots themselves, and then repeats the dispute about how much water to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that the pot itself is a problem, even with nothing inside it. The urine can be fixed by adding water, but the pot cannot be fixed that way. The amount dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי זכאי appears again inside this ברייתא.

keyTerms.term: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן כְּלוּם
keyTerms.meaning: Even though there is nothing in them

steps.confusionAlert: Adding water helps for the urine itself. It does not make an empty chamber pot acceptable.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵי רַגְלַיִם —
phrases.english: A pot for feces and a vessel for urine:
it is forbidden to read קריאת שמע facing them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: even if there is nothing in them.
And urine itself:
it is forbidden until he pours water into it.
And how much water must he pour into it?
Any amount.
Rabbi Zakkai says: a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵי רַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a fuller ברייתא that includes the amount dispute from step 26 and adds the rule about pots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A chamber pot forbids קריאת שמע even when empty. Urine is allowed once water is added, either any amount or a רביעית.

steps.title: Does it matter where the pot is in the room?
steps.stepSummary: The first view says the rule is the same whether the pot is in front of or behind the bed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says behind the bed is fine, but in front one must move four אמות away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says even in a large house one may not read until the pot is taken out or put under the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule is the same whether it is in front of the bed or behind the bed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Behind the bed, he may read. In front of the bed, he may not read, but he moves four אמות away and reads. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even in a house of one hundred אמות, he may not read until he takes them out or puts them under the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the question of the pot's location in the room. Three opinions are given: the first view makes no distinction, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is more lenient behind the bed, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the strictest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view does not distinguish between in front of the bed and behind it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient behind the bed, and in front of it he lets one read after moving four אמות away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the strictest: distance does not help even in a very big house, so the pot must be removed or hidden under the bed.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of one hundred אמות, a very big room

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. The first view treats both places the same. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient behind the bed and allows reading in front of it after moving four אמות away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires the pot to be taken out or placed under the bed.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה בֵּין לְאַחַר הַמִּטָּה.
phrases.english: Whether in front of the bed or behind the bed.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Behind the bed, he may read.
In front of the bed, he may not read.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַרְחִיק הוּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.english: But he moves four cubits away and reads.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even in a house of one hundred cubits,
he may not read until he takes them out
or puts them under the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה בֵּין לְאַחַר הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 30 and adds the question of the pot's location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first view treats in front of and behind the bed the same. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows reading behind the bed, and in front of it after moving four אמות away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires removing the pot or placing it under the bed.

steps.title: What exactly did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of two readings of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule is correct: the lenient reading or the strict reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what does he mean? Does he mean that behind the bed one reads right away, and in front of the bed one moves four אמות away and reads? Or does he mean that behind the bed one moves four אמות away and reads, and in front of the bed one does not read at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is unsure how to read רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words from the last ברייתא, so it lays out two possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lenient reading, a pot behind the bed is no problem at all, and a pot in front only needs ארבע אמות of distance. In the strict reading, everything moves one level stricter: behind the bed needs ארבע אמות, and in front of the bed one may not read at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the students in the ישיבה)
How does he mean it? What is he actually saying?
He does not read at all

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
How does he mean it?
Behind the bed, he reads right away;

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה — מַרְחִיק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: in front of the bed, he moves four cubits away and reads?
Or perhaps this is what he says:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר הַמִּטָּה — מַרְחִיק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: Behind the bed, he moves four cubits away and reads;
in front of the bed, he does not read at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion from step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule the lenient version (behind: right away; front: ארבע אמות) or the strict version (behind: ארבע אמות; front: not at all)?

steps.title: A second ברייתא settles the question
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the lenient opinion (behind the bed: read right away; in front: move ארבע אמות away). This shows the lenient reading is a real opinion, so the first reading is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: behind the bed, one reads right away; in front of the bed, one moves four אמות away. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even in a house of a hundred אמות, one may not read until he takes them out or puts them under the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that spells out the lenient opinion in clear words, which answers the question from step 32.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא states the lenient opinion openly: behind the bed is fine right away. The strict opinion here, that even a huge house does not help, matches what step 31 gave to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. So the same two opinions appear again, and the lenient one is clearly the first reading from step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא is bringing a source to answer the question
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A house a hundred אמות big, meaning a very large house
Until he takes them out of the room

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get thrown by the names. In this ברייתא the lenient view has רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's name, but in step 31 the same view had רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's name. The גמרא deals with that in the next step.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Behind the bed, he reads right away;
in front of the bed, he moves four cubits away.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even in a house of a hundred cubits,
he may not read until he takes them out
or puts them under the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lenient reading is correct: behind the bed one reads right away, and in front of the bed one moves ארבע אמות away.

steps.title: Question answered, but the two ברייתות now clash
steps.stepSummary: The question is settled, but the two ברייתות give the same opinions under switched names.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our question is answered, but the ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the question is solved, then points out a new problem: the two ברייתות do not agree about who said what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא (step 31), רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict. In the second ברייתא (step 33), the names are reversed. Both cannot be accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: Our question has been answered for us

phrases.english: Our question has been answered for us,
but the ברייתות contradict each other:

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעְיָין אִיפְּשִׁיטָא לַן, מַתְנְיָיתָא קַשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 33 but notes that it creates a conflict with step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות in steps 31 and 33.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each ברייתא gives the lenient and strict opinions to opposite תנאים, so they contradict each other.

steps.title: Swap the names in the second ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the clash by reversing the names in the later ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse the later one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction simply: switch the names in the second ברייתא so it matches the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names in the second ברייתא are switched, both sources agree: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict. This also fits the answer we just got, that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: The later one, meaning the second ברייתא

phrases.english: Reverse the later one.
phrases.notes: He means: switch the two names in the second ברייתא, the one from step 33.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names in one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about who held which opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later ברייתא has the names reversed. Switch them, and both sources say רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient.

steps.title: Why switch the second ברייתא and not the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the fix: there is no clear reason to switch the later ברייתא rather than the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you reverse the later one? Reverse the first one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own answer and asks why we picked the second ברייתא to change. This sets up the next move in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we switched the first ברייתא instead, the contradiction would also go away, but then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would hold the strict view. That would also undo the answer to the question in step 32, so the גמרא needs a reason to prefer one choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? What is your reason for choosing this?
The first one, meaning the first ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: Which ברייתא gets switched decides whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient or strict, so the practical ruling depends on it.

phrases.english: What did you see that made you reverse the later one?
Reverse the first one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה חָזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ בָּתְרָיְיתָא? אֵיפוֹךְ קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice in step 35 to switch the names in the later ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Switching the first ברייתא would remove the contradiction just as well, so choosing the second one needs a reason.

steps.title: Why the later ברייתא is the one reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the later ברייתא must be reversed, because only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is known for treating an entire house like ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have you heard say that a whole house counts as ארבע אמות? That is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. So the strict view belongs to him, and the later ברייתא is the one with the names switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 36. We know which ברייתא to fix because the strict view matches what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in other places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view says you cannot read while the excrement is anywhere in the house, so it treats the whole house like one ארבע אמות area. That idea is known as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view elsewhere. So the later ברייתא, which gives the strict view to someone else, is the one that must be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard (say this)? A way of naming the תנא known for a certain view
Four אמות, the standard 'personal area' around a person

steps.whatToRemember: The later ברייתא is the one reversed, because the 'whole house is like ארבע אמות' view belongs to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
that an entire house is considered like four אמות?
It is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36 by justifying why the later ברייתא is reversed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution based on a known view of the תנא elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either ברייתא could be the one reversed, so the fix seems random.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict 'whole house' view is known to be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's, so the later ברייתא is the one to switch.

steps.title: רב יוסף's question: how high must the bed be?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that he asked רב הונא about excrement under a bed. Below three טפחים, the bed clearly counts as touching the ground. What about three to nine טפחים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I asked רב הונא. If the bed is less than three טפחים off the ground, it is obvious to me that it counts as touching the ground. But what is the law at three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine טפחים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens about excrement under a bed. רב יוסף asks at what height the bed stops 'covering' what is beneath it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of לבוד, a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed. So a low bed is like solid ground, and the excrement under it is as if covered. The question is whether a higher bed, from three to nine טפחים, still separates the excrement from the person.

keyTerms.meaning: Connected: a gap under three טפחים is treated as if closed

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
I asked a question of רב הונא:
A bed less than three [טפחים off the ground],
it is obvious to me that it counts as connected [to the ground].
Three, four, five, six,
seven, eight, nine: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related question: the ברייתא allowed placing the pots under the bed, so how high may the bed be and still count as covering what is beneath it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a bed three to nine טפחים high separates the excrement beneath it from the person reciting.

steps.title: רב הונא does not know, but ten is clear
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that he does not know the law for three to nine טפחים. At ten טפחים, though, he has no doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know. But about ten, I certainly have no question.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא admits he cannot answer the middle heights. He adds that ten טפחים is not in doubt for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not solved, but its edges become clear. Below three is clear, and ten is clear. Only the range in between stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.
About ten, I certainly have no question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא's reply to רב יוסף's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three to nine טפחים is unknown. Ten טפחים is certain.

steps.title: אביי: ten טפחים is a separate area
steps.stepSummary: אביי agrees that ten טפחים is not a question, because any space ten טפחים high is its own separate area.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You did well not to have a question about it. Anything ten טפחים is a separate domain.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי supports רב הונא's statement about ten טפחים and gives the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A space ten טפחים high has the halachic status of a separate רשות. So the excrement under such a bed is in a different area from the person, and he may recite.

phrases.english: אביי said:
You did well that you did not have a question,
since anything ten [טפחים] is a separate domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains רב הונא's certainty about ten טפחים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any space ten טפחים high is a separate domain.

steps.title: רבא sums up the heights
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: under three counts as connected, ten is a separate area, and three to ten is the question that was never answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that less than three counts as connected, and ten is a separate domain. From three to ten is what רב יוסף asked רב הונא, and he did not answer it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gathers the whole discussion into one clear ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two heights now have a firm ruling: below three and at ten. The middle range is left as an unresolved question.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did not resolve it for him

steps.whatToRemember: Under three טפחים counts as connected (לבוד). Ten טפחים is a separate area. Three to ten is left unresolved.

phrases.english: רבא said: The הלכה is,
less than three counts as connected.
Ten is a separate domain.
From three until ten:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: this is what רב יוסף asked of רב הונא,
and he did not resolve it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the bed-height discussion as a ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Below three is connected, ten is a separate domain, and three to ten is unresolved.

steps.title: רב and רב יעקב: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Bali reports the same ruling in the name of רב יעקב, the son of שמואל's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. And so too, Bali said that רב יעקב, son of שמואל's daughter, said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier dispute and gives a ruling. Two אמוראים say we follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 37 placed the strict view with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Here רב, and רב יעקב through Bali, decide the practical law in his favor.

phrases.english: רב said:
The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
And so too Bali said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that רב יעקב, son of שמואל's daughter, said:
The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא dispute to give a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רבא disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling from רב, so the practical law is in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two sides. רב and רב יעקב follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and רבא does not. The גמרא leaves the two rulings side by side.

phrases.english: And רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in step 42.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רב אחאי finds a ספר תורה in the wedding room
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי's son could not complete the marriage. רב אחאי checked the room, found a ספר תורה there, and said they had put his son in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי arranged a match for his son with the family of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא. He brought him into the חופה, but things did not succeed. He went after him to check, and he saw a ספר תורה lying there. He said to them: If I had not come now, you would have endangered my son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that connects to the theme of keeping holy objects away from improper activity. It sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having marital relations in a room with an uncovered ספר תורה is forbidden. רב אחאי saw the son's failure as a sign of danger caused by the ספר תורה in the room.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged a marriage for his son
Wedding canopy, here meaning the room where the couple was

phrases.english: רב אחאי arranged a marriage for his son

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא,
phrases.english: with the family of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא.
He brought him into the חופה,
but things did not succeed.
phrases.notes: He means the son was not able to complete the marriage that night.

phrases.english: He went after him to check,
and he saw a ספר תורה lying there.
He said to them:
Had I not come now,
you would have endangered my son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about a ספר תורה in a room used for marital relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving an uncovered ספר תורה in the marriage room is dangerous.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind רב אחאי's warning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids marital relations in a house with a ספר תורה or תפילין, unless they are taken out or placed in a container inside another container.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: In a house with a ספר תורה or תפילין, it is forbidden to have marital relations there until he takes them out, or puts them in a container inside another container.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב אחאי's reaction: a ברייתא that forbids relations in such a room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two ways to make it permitted: take the holy objects out of the room, or double-cover them. A single covering is not enough. Two layers are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
A container inside a container (double covering)

steps.whatToRemember: Marital relations are forbidden in a room with a ספר תורה or תפילין unless they are removed or placed in a container inside a container.
steps.confusionAlert: One covering is not enough here. The ברייתא requires a container inside another container.

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a ברייתא]:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה אוֹ תְּפִילִּין
phrases.english: In a house that has a ספר תורה or תפילין in it,
it is forbidden to have marital relations in it
until he takes them out
or places them in a container inside a container.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בַּיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא behind רב אחאי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחאי's claim that the ספר תורה in the room endangered his son
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding relations in a house with a ספר תורה or תפילין unless removed or double-covered

steps.title: אביי: A regular case does not count as an extra container
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא's 'container inside a container' only works when the containers are not the ones normally used for the ספר תורה or תפילין. Their own regular containers, even ten of them, count as only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא only taught this about a container that is not their usual container. But for a container that is their usual container, even ten containers are treated like one container.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to the ברייתא from step 45. He explains which kind of 'container' actually counts as a second layer of covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a container inside a container is enough. אביי says a ספר תורה's or תפילין's own regular case is treated as part of the item itself, so stacking many of those does not add a new layer. To make it a real 'container inside a container', at least one covering must be something not normally used for them.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of... (a phrase that limits an earlier teaching)
A container that is not their usual container
A container that is their usual container (made for the ספר תורה or תפילין)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that more layers always help. According to אביי, ten regular תפילין cases are still only one layer. What matters is the kind of container, not the number.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical standard: for the double covering to work, one layer must be something other than the item's own regular case.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They only taught
this about a container that is not their container,
but a container that is their container —
even ten containers
are considered like one container.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the 'container inside a container' allowance from the ברייתא in step 45.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a container not normally used for the ספר תורה or תפילין counts as a separate layer. Their own regular containers, however many, count as a single container.

steps.title: רבא begins a statement about a cloak
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a new statement about a cloak. His statement continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A cloak...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: רבא begins a new statement about covering with a cloak, and the rest of his words come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After אביי's rule about which containers count, רבא brings up a cloak as another kind of covering. Only the opening word appears here, so his actual ruling is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak, a large outer garment

phrases.english: Rava said: A cloak

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a further statement about acceptable coverings, following אביי's limit in step 46.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Statement about a cloak as a covering. The ruling itself continues in the next section.
